question: Under ordinary growth a knot that owes more loose distinctions than it holds stalls the whole round, and no distinction ever gets a third holder. The third-holder study found that a birth taking a distinction already held twice is the one move a hidden excess needs. State that move as a growth law in its least form, a short knot pays the rest with shared distinctions, and class it: do old words still extend, do the recorded sources change, what do the starts that used to stall do, how many holders arise, what becomes of the tables that came from stalling, and does a change still spread at a bounded pace?
inputs: The recorded growth operator, sources, draws and structures the pre-registration names; its seeds.
forbidden_inputs: Any definition changed after a value is seen; any outcome of this study before the freeze.
primary_observable: The items named under 'Runs and stop rule' of the pre-registration.
comparators_or_controls: Ordinary growth on the same starts; the code checks of row G.
resource_budget: Each run under ten minutes and 12 GB on one CPU process.
first_executable_signal: Row G of the predictions table.
decision_rule: Each prediction is judged by its 'Fails when' column.
stop_rule: One script per test. The study stops when the five tests are done. It reports, beside the predictions, how many rounds and births under R involve a payment with a shared distinction.
nonclaims: An exploratory study on named samples and bounded sizes. A rival growth law is a scaffold and not the model; a census is finite and proves no all-size statement.
